_note: Hand-checked corrections from the gate build review (Nov 16 2026). The two French classes sit in the 'french' section, not the languages section, so the general gate teaches them — but their set problems are 'write real sentences', and keyword groups auto-extracted from the worked answers came out as accent-fold fragments no student's own sentences would contain. These capstones replace the extracted groups with the forms the homework itself demands (être / avoir, the passé composé), which is what a correct answer is made of.

capstone.q: Write five true sentences about yourself in French using être and avoir — for example "Je suis…" and "J'ai…". Say them or type them.
capstone.teach: Now the class's own problem — the one your professor set for this room. Take your time. Say it out loud or type it; either door is open.
capstone.teach2: Think about the two pillars: être for what you are, avoir for what you have. 'Je suis…' — I am. 'J'ai…' — I have. Build each sentence on one of them.
capstone.why: You are doing this because this is the class's real problem — the one your professor set. It is answered here, in session, not taken away as homework.

capstone.q: Write four sentences about what you did yesterday, in the passé composé: two with avoir, two with être. Say them or type them.
capstone.teach: Now the class's own problem — the one your professor set for this room. Take your time. Say it out loud or type it; either door is open.
capstone.teach2: Think about the shape: hier — yesterday — then the helper verb does the time-travelling: 'j'ai…' with avoir, 'je suis…' with être, and the participle carries what happened.
capstone.why: You are doing this because this is the class's real problem — the one your professor set. It is answered here, in session, not taken away as homework.

capstone.q: Build the C major scale and name its notes. Then build the three primary chords — I, IV, and V — and name the notes in each.
capstone.teach: Now the class's own problem — the one your professor set for this room. Take your time. Say it out loud or type it; either door is open.
capstone.teach2: Think about the pattern: whole, whole, half — whole, whole, whole, half. Lay it over C and the scale builds itself; the primary chords stand on the first, fourth and fifth notes.
capstone.why: You are doing this because this is the class's real problem — the one your professor set. It is answered here, in session, not taken away as homework.

add.teach: A Null Test at Galaxy Scales. Its stated result: For the solar neighbourhood and the local Galactic disc, the computed local density of 6.77 times ten to the -21 kg/m3 gives a fractional torsion correction of 6.96 times ten to the -79 on the neutron branch and 2.35 times ten to the -72 on the electron branch.
add.teach2: The same result, its key figure in plain figures: the computed local density is 6.77 × 10^-21 kg per cubic metre. Say that density back to me, in figures, any honest form.
add.q: For the solar neighbourhood, what computed local density does that paper report (in kg per cubic metre)?
add.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
